scope: Every printed form/phrase aligned to an English gloss in the three-page interlinear specimen. Repeated words and phrases remain separate attestation rows; no deduplication performed.
exclusions: Section titles and geographic/family headings are source metadata, not lexical units.
Quotation marks and terminal punctuation are excluded from form strings; semantic English parenthetical content remains in gloss.

Native-script pages are the same specimen in another representation, not an additional unglossed lexical corpus. Native spelling was checked against passage order but has not been falsely claimed as a character-by-character diplomatic transcription.

anchors: Two sons and the younger son requests his share.
Division and departure; wastage, famine, swine feeding, hunger.
Return, repentance, clothing, ring and shoes, feast.
Elder son in the field; hears singing and dancing; asks what is happening.
Servant answers that the brother has returned.
Elder son protests years of service and no kid for his friends.
Father replies that the son is always with him and his brother has returned to life.

transcription_notes: English hyphens preserve the source alignment, not inferred lexical segmentation.
Source putr at p592-l01-u01 differs from frequent put and is retained.
True stacked nasal marks are retained separately from ĕ/ŏ breves and simple macrons.
No POS/person/number tags inferred merely from English translation here; final structured grammar remains a subsequent review gate.
render_method: Existing full-page images plus bounded 300–450 dpi source crops; one reused disposable active crop.
own_review: All 42 aligned lines reread against rendered source; source-specific long vowels, breves, retroflex underdots and nasal marks checked with higher resolution for ambiguous areas. Independent fresh audit still required.
